title: Estimate the Percent of a Number
objective: I can estimate the percent of a number using benchmark percents, rounding, and compatible numbers.
model: double number line (amount above, percent below) marked in benchmark jumps of 10%, 25%, 50%, with compatible numbers chosen first

widgets.where: Practice Tab 1 (math/unit-4/4-3-practice-studio/, 'Benchmark Bar Meter') and tasks 1-6, 8
widgets.component: six Whole = N buttons; one bar marked only at 10% and 50%; six tiles that print the whole, 50%, 25%, 10%, 5% and 1% of it; typed answers to 10% of 80, 1% of 80, 5%, 25% of 120, 50% of 120, 75%, 1% -> 10%
widgets.root: setT1Whole(task.whole) runs on every task, so the benchmark values for the whole are already in the six tiles beside the question; tasks 1-5 and 8 are read-and-copy. The only control is a whole picker; there is no double number line and nothing to drag.
widgets.replacement: Replace the tile grid with a double number line (amount over percent, 0% to 100%) with draggable benchmark markers: the student drops the marker at 10% (snap), 25% or 50% and the line shows only the whole and the marker's percent; the amount under the marker is typed by the student. Hide the benchmark values until a marker is placed. Keep the 1% marker via a zoom window.

widgets.component: task 7 with the meter preset to Whole = 200
widgets.root: The meter is set to Whole = 200 (10% = 20) while the stem asks for 10% of 240 (key 24); the figure contradicts the question and the quick-buttons offer no 240. Task 8 also keeps Whole = 200 although its stem has no whole.
widgets.replacement: Preset the meter from the stem (add a Whole = 240 button, or change task 7 to 10% of 200 with key 20), and clear the meter for task 8 (no whole).

widgets.where: Practice Tab 2 (12 'power combo' problems with 10% / 5% / 25% sub-answers)
widgets.root: Exactly the keyIdea's step 2 (combine benchmarks); each strategy sub-answer is a separate typed field; values verified (12, 12, 15, 18, 6, 28, 30, 18, 28, 30, 8, 30).

widgets.where: Practice Tab 3 items t3_1-t3_4, t3_6-t3_8 (compatible numbers)
widgets.component: 'Original 29% of 41 ≈ [30% of 40, printed for the student] = ?'
widgets.root: The lesson's skill is choosing compatible numbers; the page prints the 'Compatible Rounded Form' pill (30% of 40) and the student only multiplies. No choice of benchmark or rounding is made by the student.
widgets.replacement: Show only 'Estimate 29% of 41.' Give two rows of tappable chips: percent (25% / 30% / 33%) and whole (40 / 41 / 50). The student builds the compatible pair; the checker accepts any pair with an easy benchmark step (e.g. 30% of 40, 25% of 40) and rejects 33% of 50 with a message about the missing benchmark; then the estimate is typed.

widgets.component: the Original Problem pill and the stem disagree
widgets.root: The pill reads 9.2% of 216 while the stem reads 'estimate 8.6% of 216 lbs of metal'; both round to 10% of 220, but the student sees two different problems.
widgets.replacement: Make the pill and the stem the same number (use 9.2% of 216 in both, key 22).

widgets.where: Practice Tab 4 (8: tip on $58.75, tip on $42.20, 70% of 6 GB, 28% of 52 rounded up twice, 25% off $79.99, 8% tax, 10% of $350 versus 1%, can $25 buy $29 at 19% off)
widgets.component: estimation in context, two error detectives
widgets.root: Rounding and benchmarks in the lesson's own contexts (the 6 GB phone is the worked example); keys verified (9, 8, 4.2, 20, 5). Note: 8% estimated as 10% of $50 = $5 overshoots the true $3.84 by 30%, so item 6 trains a poor estimate; 'Marcus' distractor C wrongly says 30% of 60 is 12.

widgets.where: Practice Bonus Round (gen partOf how=divide, 4 rounds)
widgets.root: Connects each benchmark to its divisor (10% = ÷ 10, 25% = ÷ 4, 1% = ÷ 100), which is the lesson's mental-math idea; tiles are generated from the numbers.

widgets.where: Challenge Tab 1 (8: 150% of 42, 210% of 90, 0.5% of 820, 0.8% of 500, 125% of 76, 310% of 40, 0.25% of 1,200, 175% of 80) with a static SVG each
widgets.component: estimate with a tolerance list and a worked 'strategy' line
widgets.root: Benchmark decomposition above 100% and below 1% on bars drawn for the problem (checked: 100% + 50%, half of 1%); tolerance lists accept both the exact and the rounded estimate. The strategy line is shown after the attempt.

widgets.where: Challenge Tab 2 (8 over- or underestimate mc)
widgets.component: 24% of 196 as 25% of 200, 79% of 410, 20% tip on a rounded $70, 11% as 10%, 48% of 22, a guaranteed overestimate, why overestimate for tax, 9% of $510
widgets.root: Direction-of-error reasoning is the core of estimation and every key is right (50 vs 47.04, 320 vs 323.9, $14 vs $13.68, 89 under, 10 vs 10.56, $50 vs $45.90). The correct option is usually the only one with a reason attached.

widgets.component: turn a percent into a benchmark fraction and apply it to a rounded whole
widgets.root: Uses 4-2's fraction / percent equivalence (earlier lesson) with compatible wholes; all eight estimates verified (30, 100, 10, 60, 10, 100, 500, 210).

widgets.component: 128 GB phone, battery 74%, tip, laptop 24% off, fleet miles, reservoir
widgets.root: In every story the correct choice is the only one that shows its benchmark ('About 64 GB (50% of 128 GB)') while the distractors are bare numbers ('About 48 GB'), so the answer is identifiable without estimating.
widgets.replacement: Give the three choices the same shape: 'about 25% of 128', 'about 50% of 128', 'about 40% of 128', each with its value, so the student chooses the right benchmark; move the worked line into the feedback.

widgets.where: Challenge Tab 5 (10 mc quiz) and Bonus Round (gen partOf how=decimal, 4 rounds)
widgets.component: 150% of 60, 0.5% of 600, 1/3, over or under, 12.5% as 1/8, 210%, 16.7%, guaranteed underestimate, 74% of 64, 0.25% of 8,000
widgets.root: On objective; keys verified (90, 3, 1/3, over by 1, 20, 105, 7, 75% of 90, 48, 20).

typography: Practice Tab 4 problem 8 and its hint print '$30 - $6 = $24' with a hyphen-minus
Practice Tab 5 question 7 prints the choice '50% - 10%' with a hyphen-minus
Challenge Tab 1 strategy lines print '160 - 20 = 140' and '240 - 30 = 210' with hyphen-minus
